newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SPANISH VETERAN BAKERO HEADING FOR BORO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH VETERAN BAKERO HEADING FOR BORO.

text.p: Middlesbrough are to offer Spain's former captain Jose Bakero a permanent contract, manager Bryan Robson said on Saturday.

Bakero, 33, who played for Barcelona for 16 years, is currently on trial with Middlesbrough but Robson said: "He has impressed me greatly already and could be a great driving force in our bid to get straight out of the first division."
Bakero was released on a free transfer by Mexican club Vera Cruz and has been training with Middlesbrough at their pre-season camp in Italy.

Middlesbrough are re-building with the intent of winning immediate promotion back to the premier league and following the sale of Brazilian Juninho have signed Paul Merson from Arsenal for 5.0 million pounds ($8.5 million).
But while Merson has already signed up and Bakero looks set to join him in the north-east, Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli appears not to be leaving just yet.
Ravanelli's 7.5 million pounds ($12.7 million) move from Middlesbrough to Everton appeared to be in considerable doubt on Saturday with conflicting reports coming from the Italian striker's camp.

Although Everton have had a 7.5 million bid accepted by Middlesbrough, and Ravanelli's agent Alessandro Moggi said the 28-year-old was "honoured" by the Goodison club's interest, Ravanelli himself gave the strongest hint yet he would not sign for Everton.
"There is only one club I will return to England for, and that's Liverpool," he said.
"I am flattered by Everton's interest but I don't think it would be in my best interests to join them," he told The Sun newspaper.
Liverpool have dropped their interest, after failing to agree a price with Boro.
Meanwhile Everton boss Howard Kendall confirmed: "I was in contact with his agent last night, and he was making contact with the player."

Meanwhile, Sheffield United are to sue Kendall, their former manager, and Everton with officials at Bramall Lane accusing Everton of backing out of a gentleman's agreement over compensation when Kendall moved to Goodison Park last month.
United's chief executive Charles Green said his club had appointed solicitors, consulted a top barrister and on Friday issued a writ and legal proceedings against Everton and Kendall.
Green said: "I am very annoyed that Everton have been extremely slow and unforthcoming.

"They have not fulfilled the promises that were made when we initially gave permission for Everton to approach Howard Kendall. I feel that the only way forward now is for lawyers to resolve the situation."
